title: Guard outage fail-open silently strips tools/secrets from every consumer decision (connector + docs)
reasoning: Dogfood 2026-10-02 (real use: CLI+HTTP+Python connector, fresh-box install leg). On guard unavailability the Python connector with fail_mode='open' returns Verdict(route=review, constraints={}, errored=True) so v.deliver is False — the documented consumer pattern in docs/ADOPTION.md (task.tools = [] if not v.allows_tools; task.secrets = [] if not v.allows_secrets) then silently strips tools AND secrets from EVERY task for the whole outage, turning fail-open into fail-crippled. README says fail-open means 'delivery continues flagged' but constraints={} zeroes capabilities with no signal a consumer is likely to check (deliver is the documented binding key). Fix direction: fail-open error verdicts should carry constraints with allow_* = true-with-flag (matching 'delivery continues flagged') OR ADOPTION.md must teach consumers to branch on v.errored before honouring constraints; add a connector test asserting the outage verdict's fields. Repro: Guard(endpoint='http://127.0.0.1:1', fail_mode='open').check('x') -> deliver False, allows_tools False, errored True.

title: normalizations field is misdocumented: rot13 stamped on every result, not 'why it was caught'
reasoning: Dogfood 2026-10-02. README documents normalizations as 'why it was caught, visibly', but expandRot13 (normalize.go:152-155) is applied UNCONDITIONALLY to every message and the rot13 label lands in Result.normalizations on benign deliver routes too (measured: 'plain text with no encoding at all' -> route deliver with normalizations=[rot13]; every probe run showed it). A consumer cannot distinguish 'payload was decoded' from 'label noise'; the field loses its audit value exactly when it matters. Fix direction: only report a normalization in normalizations when the DECODED variant was what drove the verdict (or split into applied[] vs load-bearing[]); update README field doc to match whichever semantic is chosen. Note: the unconditional application itself is deliberate and measured (bare ROT13 payload scored 0.32 delivered before the fix) — do not remove the transform, fix the reporting.

title: chaos-errorpath: missing config exits rc=0 with fail-closed JSON — no usage/error surface, exit code lies to callers
reasoning: QA foreman cycle 2026-10-02 — fresh-system battery on dedi-2 (chaos-errorpath cell, agent cca2210e). With no config/env on a clean machine, guardd exits rc=0 printing {"decision":"block","risk_level":"medium","route":"quarantine","reason":"guard_error (fail-closed): no openrouter api key available",...}. The fail-closed DECISION is correct design, but the PROCESS exit code is 0 — shell/CI callers keying on rc (the standard errorpath contract: clean usage = rc!=0) see success. A wrapper that only checks rc, or that greps stderr for errors, treats a broken (keyless) deployment as healthy; the failure is only visible if the caller parses the JSON body's decision field. rc=0 is reasonable for a SERVING guard (decision block is the product), but the battery grades the CLI errorpath and the exit code does not distinguish 'classified' from 'config broken'.
review_notes: Repro (agent, /tmp/qa-guard-20261002/logs/ep.log): rc=0 + fail-closed JSON. Alternative reading: rc=0 IS the intended contract (exit code = ran successfully; callers must read decision). If so, document it in README ('guardd exits 0 even when failing closed') and close the row as wontfix — but the contract is currently undocumented. Acceptance: either README documents the exit-code contract, or guardd exits nonzero when guard_error (fail-closed) fired with no key configured.
